title: Decompose 15 oversize Python source files to clear the file-size allowlist
summary: Architecture analysis for the 15-file decomposition program. Confirms the refine-phase recommendation (A1+B2+C1) survives implementation-level scrutiny, locks the per-file submodule cluster boundaries, identifies the production importers and 34 distinct test patch targets that the re-export barrel must preserve, and resolves the routes-registration question (existing Blueprint, not @app.route — decision-8's wrappers stay in __init__.py). Output drives the task_planner and risk_analyst.

problem_statement.description: The lint added by #2250 caps Python source files at 1,500 lines / 100 KB. Fifteen files are grandfathered in scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml. This issue tracks the program that drives those baselines to zero so every file is under the global cap, the allowlist is empty, and agent navigation cost is paid once instead of per BRC cycle. Pure refactor — no behavior change.
goals: All 15 files under 1,500 lines AND 100 KB
scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml empty (or only contains entries unrelated to this issue)
Zero behavior change; make lint and make test-all green at every slice boundary
No production importer breaks; no test patch target moves out from under existing tests
Decomposition seams documented in orchestrator/CLAUDE.md and gateway/CLAUDE.md so the next contributor knows where pieces live
non_negotiables: Test back-compat via re-exports — 34 distinct symbols are patched at routes.pipelines.<sym>; gateway.gateway and mcp_tools have similar surfaces.
External importers preserved — mcp_tools, unified_sse, routes/decisions, routes/phases, api.py all reach into routes.pipelines today.
Dual-import convention preserved at boundary; submodules use one consistent style internally.
Allowlist ratchet — each PR drops the affected file's entry; lint enforces.

recommended_approach.name: Sub-package + barrel + per-phase _run_pipeline + 1+15 slice forest
recommended_approach.summary: Per refine and HITL: each oversize file becomes a sub-package <name>/ with an __init__.py barrel that explicitly re-exports every symbol the test suite or production code currently reaches at the original module path. Submodules are underscore-prefixed (`_run_loop.py`, `_criteria.py`, `_pr_lifecycle.py`, ...). _run_pipeline is decomposed into per-phase handlers (refine/plan/implement/pr) plus a thin orchestration loop in slice-16. Slices land as one parent (slice-1: docs + scripts/select_tests.py reference) plus 15 sibling children, fanned out smallest-first under EGG_ORCH_MAX_PARALLEL_SLICES=5 (3 waves of 5).
rationale: Sub-package + explicit re-export barrel (A1 + decision-5) is the only layout that keeps unittest.mock.patch('routes.pipelines._foo') resolving without rewriting tests.
Per-phase handler refactor (B2) is the only _run_pipeline strategy that satisfies 'every file under 1,500 lines AND allowlist empty AND _run_pipeline in scope'.
16-slice forest (C1) gives one PR per file — maximum reviewability and revertibility, and the forest rule (one parent each) is satisfied by 15 siblings under one shared parent.
Smallest-first ordering validates the pattern on scripts/select_tests.py before committing to gateway.py and pipelines.py at the end.
Underscore-prefixed submodules match existing codebase convention (e.g. orchestrator/routes/_helpers.py-style internal modules) and signal 'package-private API'.
Existing Blueprint usage in routes/* and `app = Flask(...)` in gateway/ both compose cleanly with the 'thin wrappers in __init__.py' shape; no behavior-adjacent Blueprint refactor is needed.
constraints: Re-export barrel MUST list every test-patched and production-imported symbol explicitly. Drift is detectable by `git grep <symbol>` returning hits outside the new submodule that don't go through the barrel.
Each slice's PR must independently pass `make lint` (size cap, allowlist ratchet, ruff/mypy) and `make test-all` (full suite). No 'land them together' carve-outs.

scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml entry for the affected file MUST be removed (not just lowered) on the same PR that drops the file under cap. The entry has no per-file baseline today (cap-only), so removal is a one-line yaml change.
If the new submodules accidentally exceed the cap individually, the slice's task list MUST further split that submodule rather than re-introducing an allowlist entry.
Test patch path drift (Q1): only mechanical rewrites are in-scope. Test-logic rewrites are filed as follow-up issues; the same slice does NOT bundle them.

open_questions.question: Should mcp_tools.py and gateway_client.py — which are dominated by ONE big class — use composition (delegate to handler classes per submodule) or method modules (define methods at module level, attach to class via assignment)?
open_questions.context: mcp_tools.py has PipelineToolHandler with ~25 _handle_* methods spanning lines 1029-2820. gateway_client.py has GatewayClient with similar shape. The barrel option is (a) keep one class, define methods in submodules and assign at class load time, or (b) split into multiple handler classes that PipelineToolHandler composes. Option (a) preserves the existing public class shape and keeps test patches like `mcp_tools.PipelineToolHandler` resolving; option (b) is more idiomatic but changes the class hierarchy.
open_questions.recommendation: Option (a) — method modules attached to the existing class. Preserves tests; minimum behavior risk; the test surface here is tighter than in pipelines.py so we can be more aggressive. Document the pattern in docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md.

open_questions.question: Should the per-phase handlers extracted from _run_pipeline (slice-15, decision-2 B2) live as private functions in `_phase_handlers.py`, or as four separate submodules (`_phase_refine.py`, `_phase_plan.py`, `_phase_implement.py`, `_phase_pr.py`)?
open_questions.context: Each per-phase handler is estimated at 200-500 lines. A single `_phase_handlers.py` would land at 1,000-1,400 lines (under cap). Four separate submodules would each be 200-500 lines (well under cap) but adds 3 more files to the diff.
open_questions.recommendation: Start with four separate submodules. Each phase handler has independent state, error handling, and logging seams; cross-phase coupling is via the shared _PipelineRunContext. Keeps each new file small and easy to review independently. Submodules: orchestrator/routes/pipelines/_phase_refine.py, _phase_plan.py, _phase_implement.py, _phase_pr.py.

open_questions.question: When a proposed submodule lands AT or OVER the 1,500-line cap, should slice-15 (pipelines.py) further split it as a sub-task in the same slice, or should slice-15 declare a sub-slice (slice-15a, slice-15b)?
open_questions.context: decision-9 selected 'single slice with multiple commits/sub-tasks' over a chain of sub-slices. So further splitting stays inside slice-15's branch as additional commits. The risk_analyst should weigh the size of slice-15's PR against revertibility.
open_questions.recommendation: Further splits stay as sub-tasks within slice-15 (per decision-9). If slice-15's PR becomes too large to review (~5,000+ lines diff), the implementer can stack PRs along slice-15's branch (slice-15a → slice-15b → slice-15c → main of stack), all targeting the slice-15 integration branch which itself targets main. This keeps the slice-DAG forest rule intact (one parent: slice-1) while letting reviewers see internally-stacked PRs.

open_questions.question: Should the barrel __init__.py also re-export Pipeline-private constants like PHASE_TRANSITIONS, _PIPELINE_RUNTIME_STATE module globals, etc.?
open_questions.context: Tests reach module-level attributes like `routes.pipelines._inflight_host_waits` — these are dicts/sets, not functions. A re-export of `from ._mod import _inflight_host_waits` will re-bind the name to the same object, but if the submodule rebinds it (e.g. `_inflight_host_waits = {}`), the barrel's reference becomes stale. This is a test-fragility risk.
open_questions.recommendation: For mutable module-level state used by tests (counter dicts, in-flight tracking, etc.), keep the canonical instance defined in the submodule and have the barrel re-export it. NEVER reassign the name in either place after module load. Document this rule in docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md. risk_analyst should verify that no submodule rebinds a re-exported name.

open_questions.question: Where should slice-1 commit the slice-DAG plan itself? The plan-phase contract emits slices into the contract YAML, not into a markdown file. Does the contract need any special ordering metadata for the 15 sibling children to fan out smallest-first?
open_questions.context: Per Q3 feedback, slices fan out smallest-first. The slice-DAG document describes 'Wave' as 'a set of slices whose dependencies are all satisfied'. With one parent and 15 siblings, the scheduler will naturally pull all 15 into wave 2 with concurrency 5. Smallest-first is achieved by listing them in size order in the contract; the scheduler picks them up in declaration order.
open_questions.recommendation: task_planner emits slices in the contract in size-ascending order (smallest first). No new metadata needed — the existing FIFO scheduling under EGG_ORCH_MAX_PARALLEL_SLICES is sufficient.

risk_assessment_seeds.risk: Test patch path drift — a moved symbol's re-export shim is forgotten, causing AttributeError in unittest.mock.patch resolution.
risk_assessment_seeds.mitigation_seed: Each slice's task list MUST include a `git grep <symbol>` audit before merging to ensure every patch target still resolves through the barrel. Add a CI check that errors on missing barrel re-exports if feasible (e.g. compare barrel __all__ to submodule symbols).

risk_assessment_seeds.risk: _run_pipeline per-phase refactor introduces a subtle ordering bug (race condition, missed respawn, mis-ordered teardown).
risk_assessment_seeds.mitigation_seed: Slice-15 lands LAST after pattern is proven on 14 simpler files. The PR runs `make test-all` and the integration test suite.
